F1: The null only comes back for a group that was deleted while the request was running, which is the race this change fixes; its only caller just copies it onto a representation of the vanished group, so nothing is functionally harmed.
F2: This is test cleanup for a failure path: if a `remove()` throws, the test fails anyway, and the surefire fork exits, so a non-daemon thread won't hang the build.
F3: Not joining the reader and having no success counter only weakens the test; across 100 HTTP deletes the reader will almost certainly run many reads, so this is not a defect.
